questions.question: What is weathering? Name three things that cause it.
questions.expected_answer: Weathering is the breaking down of rock into smaller pieces. It is caused by heating and cooling, which makes rock expand and shrink until it cracks; water freezing in cracks and pushing them wider; plant roots growing into cracks; and moving water and wind wearing rock away.

questions.question: Describe the three layers of a soil profile.
questions.expected_answer: Topsoil is the top layer. It is dark, loose and crumbly, with lots of humus, roots and living things. Subsoil is below it. It is paler, with little humus, bigger pieces of rock and fewer living things. At the bottom is solid rock, which the soil came from.

questions.question: Explain how topsoil forms and why it is precious.
questions.expected_answer: Weathering breaks rock into smaller and smaller grains. Living things such as earthworms, fungi and bacteria break down dead plants and animals into humus, which mixes with the rock grains, and plants grow and add more humus. This slowly builds topsoil. It takes hundreds of years to form just a few centimetres, so topsoil is precious.
